archetype.name: Pocket Passer (high-volume, short-area)
archetype.definition: A big-bodied second-year starter who wins from the pocket on volume and short-to-intermediate timing throws. He creates little outside structure beyond the odd well-chosen scramble, and his line is shaped as much by attempts as by efficiency.

report.headline: Volume props up a league-average passer whose screens and fumbles drain value
report.take:
Shough is a 39-attempt-a-game quarterback on a 2-5 team whose defense ranks 26th in EPA. That combination explains most of his box score. He ranks 14th in passing yards per game and is on a 4,180-yard, 32-touchdown pace. The efficiency underneath is ordinary: 6.3 yards per attempt (34th of 47), +0.018 EPA per dropback (25th), and a CPOE just below zero. He is a volume passer first, and the volume comes from game script and a staff that passes slightly more than situation predicts.

The depth splits are where the story gets interesting. Every charted throw past the line of scrimmage is positive. Short throws (0-9 air yards) run +0.203 EPA, intermediate +0.376 and deep +0.303, with his 10-plus-yard throws as a group at +0.349 per attempt. The hole is the 45 throws behind the line, which cost -19.6 EPA. That one bucket erases most of what his downfield work builds, and much of it is play-calling rather than his arm. Under center he has been sharp at +0.20 a play, and shotgun is slightly negative. Both are worth noting given the small under-center sample.

Two things the averages hide. First, the sack avoidance is a real change. Last year his pressure-to-sack rate was 41.9%, 48th of 62. This year it is 24.6%, 15th of 38, and his sack rate of 5.2% sits under the league's 6.9%. Second, ball security has gone the other way. Three lost fumbles rank 43rd of 47, and six fumbles are charted as turnover-worthy alongside six interceptions. His bad-throw rate (15.4%, 29th of 38) is almost identical to last year's. Spotty ball placement looks like who he is, not a slump.

The recent stretch is rougher than the season line. Over the last three games his CPOE is -7.3, he is at 5.57 yards per attempt, and his interception rate is up a point. That stretch includes a -11.9 EPA game against Minnesota's top-ranked defense and a 16-of-30 day against the Giants. Fantasy-wise, three touchdowns and a rushing score covered for that Giants game. Then Week 7 against Pittsburgh's sixth-ranked defense was his best passing day, at +10.6 EPA on 30-of-38. His week-to-week variance is enormous, but the floor and ceiling have both shown up against good defenses.

strengths.title: Downfield throws are carrying the efficiency
strengths.body: Once the ball travels past the line, he is consistently positive: +0.376 EPA on intermediate throws and +0.303 deep, with the 10-plus group at +0.349. A deep completion rate around 38% is normal for that depth. The bigger point is that the EPA holds up without a pile of interceptions. The deep sample is only 29 attempts, so the exact rate is soft, but the intermediate work has been steady enough to trust.

strengths.title: Sack avoidance has genuinely improved
strengths.body: His pressure-to-sack rate fell from 41.9% last year, near the bottom of the league, to 24.6% now. That came with a nearly identical time to throw, so this looks like faster processing under duress rather than quicker designs. A ninth-ranked offensive hit rate helps, but the change shows up in his own per-pressure number, which makes it more likely to stick.

strengths.title: Olave and Vele are a productive pair
strengths.body: His two primary wideouts are producing at strong rates: Olave at +0.528 EPA per target on 71 targets and Vele at +0.46 on 48. The offense works when the ball goes to them. That is a stable, repeatable base as long as both stay healthy.

concerns.title: Ball security is a real problem
concerns.body: He has three lost fumbles (43rd of 47) and six turnover-worthy fumbles to go with six interceptions. Lost-fumble totals carry some luck and should cool. The underlying fumble count is not luck, though, and his interception rate has climbed over the last three games. For a team with a bottom-tier defense, giving away possessions is the costliest thing he does.

concerns.title: Screens and long third downs drag the offense
concerns.body: The 45 throws behind the line cost -19.6 EPA, and third downs are -0.173 a play with an average of 8.4 yards to go. The first is mostly scheme and the second is the result of failed early downs. Neither is purely on him. They do cap his efficiency unless the staff cuts the screen volume or the 24th-ranked run game starts winning first down.

concerns.title: Accuracy has slipped and stayed loose
concerns.body: His CPOE fell 2.3 points from last year, and the last three games sit at -7.3. His bad-throw rate is unchanged from 2025 and ranks 29th of 38. That suggests his placement was never pinpoint, and the positive CPOE he had last year was the outlier. Meanwhile, a +10.1 red-zone CPOE is producing most of his touchdowns, which is unlikely to hold.

trend.note: His passing EPA has swung from +10.9 against Baltimore to -11.9 against Minnesota and back to +10.6 against Pittsburgh, with near-zero games in between. The last three games are worse on accuracy and yardage, but the most recent outing was his cleanest.

nextGame.headline: Rested Saints face a stingy Cleveland pass defense at home
nextGame.body:
Cleveland's defense is built to make his game hard. It ranks 7th in pass EPA, 8th in both hit rate and sack rate, and 9th on deep throws, and it has allowed the 5th-fewest quarterback yards per game. The soft spot is the run: 28th in rush EPA and last in explosive runs allowed. Offenses lean on the ground against them, with a pass rate 1.4 points below their norm, 24th. Tight ends have gone nowhere, at -0.16 EPA per target (2nd), which takes Juwan Johnson's routes off the menu. Third receivers have feasted, though, and that is a possible outlet if a slot option emerges. The likely script is a game where New Orleans runs more and Shough throws less, with the Saints favored by 2.5 and the total at 43.5. That points to fewer attempts than his usual 39.

Availability on his side matters. Guard Cesar Ruiz, a 90%-snap starter, is questionable with a knee injury against a front that gets home. Running backs Travis Etienne (IR, hamstring) and CJ Donaldson (shoulder) are both uncertain, and that bears directly on whether the Saints can exploit Cleveland's weak run defense. Jordyn Tyson's practice window may open, but he has not played. Cleveland lists no injuries. Coming off the bye with 14 days of rest, indoors, there are no conditions excuses either way.

keyMatchups.title: His pocket versus Cleveland's pressure
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland ranks 8th in both hit rate and sack rate, and Ruiz's knee could weaken the interior. His improved pressure-to-sack rate is exactly the skill being tested. Throwaways and checkdowns under pressure are fine; fumbles in the pocket are not.

keyMatchups.title: Run funnel versus a weak run game
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland is a run funnel that ranks 28th against the run. The Saints' rushing offense is only 24th in EPA, and two backs are banged up. If the ground game finally wins early downs, his third-and-long problem eases. If it doesn't, he is left throwing into a top-10 pass defense in obvious passing situations.

keyMatchups.title: Olave against a solid secondary
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland has held opposing WR1s slightly under their averages and is 14th in EPA allowed to them, middle of the pack rather than shutdown. With the tight end matchup closed, Olave's +0.528 per target is the most efficient path to points.

nextGame.watch: Whether the bye produces fewer screens and more true quick-game throws past the line. Week 7's short, efficient approach worked, and his two best games both came on his lowest-aDOT nights.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is the sustainable part. A defense ranked 26th will keep forcing the Saints to throw, and the staff already leans pass. Expect him to stay in the low-to-mid 200s in yards most weeks even if efficiency stays flat. His improved sack avoidance looks real, and the Olave/Vele pairing gives him a reliable base. The touchdown rate is the part to fade. A +10.1 red-zone CPOE is carrying a lot of it, and his league-average EPA doesn't support a 32-touchdown pace. Something closer to 1.2-1.8 touchdowns a game is the honest range.

Lost fumbles should cool somewhat, but the underlying fumble and bad-throw numbers say turnovers will remain part of the package. The game-to-game swings will continue. Weeks of +10 EPA and weeks near -12 are both in his range, and the opponent's pass rush seems to matter more than its overall ranking. Upside comes from the staff trimming screen volume, since his downfield work is genuinely good. Downside comes from more Minnesota-style games against fronts that collapse the pocket.
swingFactors: Screen and behind-the-line volume in the play-calling
Etienne's return and a run game that wins early downs
Fumble and interception rate under pressure

confidence.note: Seven starts with wild week-to-week swings. Volume is stable, but efficiency and touchdown rate rest on small, noisy splits.
